::: {#exm-map-beta-bernoulli}
#### The MAP estimate of a proportion

In [the Beta-Bernoulli example](bayesian-inference.qmd#exm-beta-bernoulli),
the posterior of $\prob$ after $r$ successes in $n$ trials is
$\operatorname{Beta}(a + r,\; b + n - r)$.
Write $\shape = a + r$ and $\shapeb = b + n - r$ for its two parameters.
For $\shape, \shapeb > 1$, the log of the posterior density, up to a constant, is
$(\shape - 1)\log \prob + (\shapeb - 1)\log(1 - \prob)$.
Setting its derivative with respect to $\prob$ to zero gives

$$
\ba
0
&= \frac{\shape - 1}{\prob} - \frac{\shapeb - 1}{1 - \prob}
&& \text{(derivative of the log density)}\\
0
&= (\shape - 1)(1 - \prob) - (\shapeb - 1)\prob
&& \text{(multiplying by $\prob(1-\prob)$)}\\
(\shape - 1)(1 - \prob)
&= (\shapeb - 1)\prob
&& \text{(adding $(\shapeb - 1)\prob$ to both sides)}\\
(\shape - 1) - (\shape - 1)\prob
&= (\shapeb - 1)\prob
&& \text{(expanding the product on the left)}\\
\shape - 1
&= (\shape - 1)\prob + (\shapeb - 1)\prob
&& \text{(adding $(\shape - 1)\prob$ to both sides)}\\
\shape - 1
&= (\shape + \shapeb - 2)\prob
&& \text{(collecting the terms in $\prob$)},
\ea
$$

so $\hparam_{\text{MAP}} = \frac{\shape - 1}{\shape + \shapeb - 2}$.
With the uniform prior $\operatorname{Beta}(1, 1)$,
$r = 55$ successes and $n = 91$ trials,
the posterior is $\operatorname{Beta}(56, 37)$.
Its mode and its mean are:

```{r}
#| label: map-beta-bernoulli
#| code-fold: false
a_post <- 1 + 55
b_post <- 1 + 91 - 55
c(
  mode = (a_post - 1) / (a_post + b_post - 2),
  mean = a_post / (a_post + b_post)
) |>
  round(3)
```

The mode equals the sample proportion $r / n$,
because the uniform prior adds no pseudo-counts that pull it away.
The mean is a little closer to $\frac{1}{2}$.
:::
